repository_dependencies: MATLAB for some figure 4 network efficiency/BAS analysis

experiment_profile.host: Daucus carota in-vitro root organ culture
experiment_profile.geometry: split Petri plate; root compartment separated from fungus-only compartment; 2D constrained growth imaging
experiment_profile.typical_imaging: about 150 images per replicate at 2-hour intervals
experiment_profile.replicates: up to 40 in vitro ROC plant-fungal replicates; figure-specific graph statistics report 12 replicates
experiment_profile.flow_recording: bright-field microscopy at 20-25 frames per second for 20-60 seconds

reported_observations_to_reproduce: growing-tip pulse ahead of trailing hyphal filament-density wave
approximately translating front and saturating trailing filament density
density regulation associated with hyphal fusion/anastomosis
root-directed network efficiency remains approximately constant while global efficiency increases
edge radius correlates with betweenness centrality
early tipward velocity about 30 percent faster; directional bias falls below significance around day 10
average flow speeds are stable over about 20 days while network length grows by nearly two orders of magnitude
evidence_limits: full graph extraction was enabled by constraining growth to 2D; it is not a 3D soil reconstruction
flow videos cover selected ROIs and manually screened maximum-speed outliers
strain and species coverage is limited to the three named AMF profiles
flow, graph efficiency, nutrient delivery and plant uptake are separate observables
claim_ceiling: This source can qualify a 2D in-vitro AMF graph and flow benchmark. It does not establish 3D soil networks, all fungal guilds, universal trade strategies or a general fungal transport law.
